angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 274,106 km at 87.23 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 11.4641 +/- 0.0258 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 87.23 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.394 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Kanodia et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5205 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract): 274,106 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.392 +/- 0.015 solar masses from Kanodia et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5205 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3430 +/- 54 K from Kanodia et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5205 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kanodia et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5205 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5205.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.840, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5205 (pscomppars): spectral type M4.0, from Kanodia et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5205 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0 dex, from Kanodia et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5205 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.7122, from Kanodia et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5205 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 2 km/s, from Kanodia et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..120K/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
